title: Movie Crush: Janet Varney on Tron
summary: Pilot episode of Movie Crush hosted by Chuck Bryant (with Josh Clark), recorded at Pone City Market in Atlanta, featuring actress and improviser Janet Varney discussing her favorite movie, Disney's Tron (1982), directed by Steven Lisberger. They cover her childhood movie-going with her dad and mom, her memories of playing the Tron arcade game and a home "inside the game grid" game with her dad, the film's history and ahead-of-its-time computer animation, the sequel Tron: Legacy, Roger Ebert's review, the 1982 movie year, and guilty pleasures such as horse movies, shark movies like Deep Blue Sea, and Intolerable Cruelty. Also touches on Twin Peaks, David Lynch, and Janet's show Stand Against Evil.

segments.title: Opening and introduction to Janet Varney
segments.summary: Chuck introduces Movie Crush episode one, his guest Janet Varney, her comedy festival Sketch Fest, and her show Stand Against Evil. They discuss how the show got its title.

segments.title: Childhood movie-going in Arizona
segments.summary: Janet recalls going to movie theaters as a kid in Arizona to escape the summer heat, riding the bus alone to see films, and a memorable viewing of Dead Poets Society.

segments.title: Twin Peaks, David Lynch and early movie influences
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Twin Peaks revival and David Lynch. Janet describes her first movies, including Robocop and Die Hard with her mom, and the movies her dad let her see such as Animal House, while her mom was strict about violence.

segments.title: Choosing a favorite movie and Janet's pick of Tron
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the difficulty of naming an all-time favorite movie. Janet previously named Harold and Maud, then chooses Tron as her pick. She admits she had never seen the film until the day of recording.

segments.title: Janet's childhood memories of the Tron arcade game and home game
segments.summary: Janet describes playing the Tron arcade game, her love of the Tron world, and a game she played with her dad at home in the dark, pretending to be inside the game grid while avoiding the recognizers. She also recalls the Tron ride at Disneyland's People Mover.

segments.title: Making of Tron and its ahead-of-its-time animation
segments.summary: They discuss Steven Lisberger's passion project, its early computer animation and rotoscoping, Disney's investment, and how the film looks today. Janet mentions Tron memorabilia and a Kubrick toy collection.

segments.title: Tron: Legacy, the cast and the story
segments.summary: Janet says she did not connect with Tron: Legacy, though she saw it once in a theater. They discuss Jeff Bridges, David Warner as the villain, the MCP and Sark, the film's abrupt opening and ending, and the company Encom.

segments.title: Roger Ebert review and the 1982 movie year
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Roger Ebert's four-star review of Tron, praising its effects. They list other major films from 1982 such as Blade Runner, E.T., The Thing, and Poltergeist, and talk about special effects today.

segments.title: Guilty pleasures: horse movies, shark movies and Cohen Brothers
segments.summary: Janet names guilty pleasures: feel-good horse movies watched on planes, shark movies such as Deep Blue Sea, and Intolerable Cruelty. The hosts discuss Snakes on a Plane and Stephen Lisberger's later work.

segments.title: Wrap-up and sign-off
segments.summary: Chuck and Janet close the first episode, Chuck praises the conversation, and he promotes Stand Against Evil and Janet's podcast J V Club before signing off.
